# Dock projection: a rejected vdom update mid-swap strands two shells in the host

## Context

Observed live on 2026-09-02 in a downstream dock workspace app (engine checkout at `dev@ec6856b804`, Chrome, shared workers), read through the Neural Link while the broken window was still open. The user had pinned a right-edge pane to its rail, pinned it back, pinned it again and pinned it back again. The dock host then held TWO projected shells:

| host child | what it held | `visibility` | x |
|---|---|---|---|
| `neo-container-21` (the outgoing shell) | every real pane: two grids, the editor pane, an emptied aux tabs container whose header had no tab button left | visible | -1397 (one host width left) |
| `neo-container-25` (the staged shell) | three tab-node placeholders (`neo-component-53/54/55`) and a fresh rail with its reveal overlay | hidden | 0 |

App-worker console, one entry, immediately followed by an unhandled-rejection report from the app's logger:

```
vdom update failed <workspace id> util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-tab-header-button-10
    at VNode.getVnode          (src/util/VNode.mjs:212)
    at VNode.createMap         (src/util/VNode.mjs:25 … :41)
    at Workspace.syncVnodeTree (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:925)
    at Workspace.afterSetVnode (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:125)
```

`neo-tab-header-button-10` was the tab button of the pane leaving for the rail. The host's `scrollLeft` was 1397 as well; that part is the preview-in-flow defect filed separately and is what made the user see an empty workspace instead of the hidden staged shell — but with the preview fixed the state above is still fatal: the shell in view is the hidden one.

## The Problem

`Reconciler.reconcileProjection` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs:341`) is a four-phase transaction, each phase `host.update(); await host.promiseUpdate()`:

1. insert the next shell hidden at `shellIndex + 1` (`:426`), commit;
2. `reconcileTabChrome` — move pane/button pairs, retire leavers (`state.bar.removeTabAt(index, true, true)` destroys the button SILENTLY, `:769-770`), commit the bars whose membership changed, hide emptied source tabs, commit;
3. `moveRetainedTabChrome`, swap shell visibility, commit;
4. `host.remove(oldShell, true, true)` (`:488`), commit.

A rejected `promiseUpdate()` anywhere after phase 1 throws out of the method. Nothing catches it: not `reconcileProjection`, not `Workspace#refreshDockWorkspace` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, the `await Reconciler.reconcileProjection(...)` at `:3525` sits outside the only `try` in that method), and `onDockZoneDocumentChange` (`:3347-3361`) puts the `.catch(() => {})` on the PREVIOUS refresh only, so the failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the host keeps both shells: the outgoing one still visible and populated, the staged one hidden and half-built. Every later commit reconciles against `host.items[shellIndex]` again, so the state does not self-heal.

The rejection itself is a stale vnode reference: `VNode.createMap` follows `{componentId}` references through the live component registry and THROWS when a referenced component is gone (`src/util/VNode.mjs:212`). Here the workspace's OWN flight landed while the aux tab bar's stored vnode still listed the button that phase 2 had just destroyed silently. Which workspace-level write opened that flight is not established — `MotionSignal.enter/leave` (`addCls`/`removeCls` of `neo-dashboard-dock-animating` on the workspace, `src/dashboard/dock/projection/MotionSignal.mjs`) is the one workspace-level vdom write on the refresh path; the timing that lands it inside a later transaction's phase 2 (a slow FLIP `played` promise reaching the 2000 ms fail-safe, or two commits inside one motion window) is the open question. The observing workspace has no vdom writes of its own on the workspace node.

Two separate headless reproductions of the same pin cycles (three cycles each, Chrome and Chromium) did not hit the rejection; the user hit it at human pace. Treat the race as intermittent and the missing failure path as deterministic.

## The Architectural Reality

- The reconciler's promise (docking design record §2.6, reparent-never-recreate) is that panes survive a re-projection by identity. A half-run transaction breaks that promise in the worst way: the panes survive, inside a shell the host will never show again.
- `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate` documents the contract on its side (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:366-395`): a rejected flight adopts no vnode and rejects every parked promise so "the next cycle re-diffs cleanly" — the dock is the caller that has to USE that cleanliness and does not.
- `isChildUpdating` / `isParentUpdating` serialize ancestor and descendant flights (`VdomLifecycle.mjs:692-745`), so the host's phase updates queue behind a workspace-level flight rather than merging into it; a silent structural removal made between two flights is exactly what a landing ancestor flight cannot know about.

## The Fix

1. **Fail-safe transaction.** In `reconcileProjection`, guard phases 2–4: on rejection, retire the staged shell if it is still hidden (or finish the swap if the retained chrome already moved), un-hide the outgoing shell, and re-throw a typed error the workspace handles by scheduling ONE clean `refreshDockWorkspace` against the committed document (the reject-then-re-diff contract above). `Workspace#refreshDockWorkspace` / `onDockZoneDocumentChange` surface the failure (a `dockProjectionFailed` event plus the existing warn path) instead of an unhandled rejection.
2. **Close the observed race** once characterized: either make the silent leaver retirement publish through the bar before an ancestor flight can land (enroll the retiring bar in `commitBars`, the way cross-bar moves already are, `Reconciler.mjs:733-740`), or let `VNode.createMap` skip a reference whose component is destroyed (the removal delta follows in the next flight) — a maintainer call between fail-loud and degrade; the ticket does not pre-empt it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit or component spec rejects one host update inside `reconcileProjection` (phase 2 and phase 3 arms) and asserts: exactly one shell in the host afterwards, visible, at `shellIndex`; every pane of the committed document reachable; the workspace's next commit reconciles normally.
- [ ] The failure is observable through an event or the workspace's warn path; no unhandled rejection.
- [ ] The stale-reference rejection is either reproduced with a red-first arm (a workspace-level cls write landing during phase 2) and closed, or characterized in the PR body with the guard from AC 1 as the shipped mitigation.
- [ ] Post-merge, hand check: three pin → rail → pin-back cycles on a right-edge pane in `apps/workstation` and in a consumer host with a heavy DOM leave one shell.

## Out of Scope

- The preview overlay's in-flow layout (separate ticket).
- FLIP timing and `MotionSignal` fail-safe duration as such.

## Related

- Epic #13158 (docking polish); the reconciler notes on in-flight collisions in `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` (search "collision that duplicated retained chrome").
- `#14911` (closed) — a destroyed child's DOM surviving a wholesale container refresh: the same family of "destroyed component still referenced by a landing tree", resolved at the container level; the dock's transaction sits one layer above it.

- 2026-09-02T22:15:29Z @tobiu referenced in commit `4d9c6b2` - "fix(dock): a rejected projection phase settles the host to one shell and reports it (#18143) (#18147)

The four-phase projection holds TWO shells for the whole window between staging
the next one and retiring the old one, and every phase ends in an awaited host
flight that can reject. Nothing caught it: not reconcileProjection, not
refreshDockWorkspace, and onDockZoneDocumentChange attaches its .catch to the
PREVIOUS refresh rather than the one it starts. So a rejection unwound out of the
method and left both shells in the host — the outgoing one visible and populated,
the staged one hidden and half-built — and since every later commit reconciles
against host.items[shellIndex] again, the state never self-healed.

VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate already promises the half this needs: a rejected
flight adopts no vnode and rejects every parked promise, so the next cycle
re-diffs cleanly. The dock was the caller that had to use that cleanliness.

Phases 2-4 are now one guarded transaction. On rejection settleFailedProjection
restores the only invariant later commits depend on — one shell, at shellIndex,
visible — choosing the survivor from the last LANDED flight rather than intent:
before the visibility swap commits the outgoing shell is on screen, after it the
staged one is. It does not rebuild content; the committed document is untouched
by a failed projection, so the repair is a clean re-projection from it.

The retired staged shell is detached but NOT destroyed. By the time most
rejections land, reconcileTabChrome has already moved live pane/button pairs into
it, and destroying it would take them with it — the exact opposite of the
reparent-never-recreate promise the transaction exists to keep. Those panes stay
alive and the repair re-parents them by identity.

The failure is re-thrown rather than wrapped, marked isDockProjectionFailure with
a projectionRecovery verdict: the original message and stack ARE the diagnostic,
and the live report that produced this guard read "Component not found for id"
out of syncVnodeTree. Workspace#onDockProjectionFailed warns, fires
dockProjectionFailed, and schedules exactly ONE repair — a second failure
surfaces without scheduling a third, so a deterministic fault cannot hot-loop."

- 2026-09-02T22:15:45Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `d284d1b` - "fix(dock): the shell the recovery detaches is destroyed once the repair empties it (#18143)

The recovery detaches a retired staged shell without destroying it, because at
that moment it still holds the live panes the repair has yet to re-parent out.
The JSDoc then claimed the repair leaves it "empty and unreferenced". Empty, yes.
Unreferenced, no: `Neo.manager.Instance.unregister` is reached from exactly one
place, `core.Base#destroy`, so a merely-detached component stays registered and
the manager holds it for the life of the app. Every un-swapped failure leaked one
registered container, permanently.

The exit was already inside the argument for detaching. The shell is dangerous to
destroy BECAUSE it holds live panes — and the repair re-parents those panes out by
identity. After the repair it holds nothing, so destroying it there takes nothing
with it and reintroduces none of the risk. The leak only ever needed to survive
until the repair completed.

So `settleFailedProjection` now returns `{recovery, retiredShell}` and hands the
detached shell back rather than dropping it, and `Workspace#retireStrandedShell`
destroys it after the repair.

Emptiness is asserted, never assumed. A repair that itself fails re-enters the
handler as a retry and still resolves, so reaching the cleanup is not proof the
panes moved. A shell that still has items is left alone: leaking one container is
cheap next to destroying live panes, which is the one outcome this entire failure
path exists to prevent.

Found by @neo-opus-ada, who took the detach-not-destroy call I asked her to
challenge, agreed with the trade, and then showed that my own reasoning contained
the close I had not taken."
